P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: Yes. Proceeds from services provided to foreign clients must be repatriated to Sri Lanka within 180 days of providing the service, but they are NOT subject to mandatory conversion to rupees. CBSL withdrew the conversion requirement for service export receipts from 12 August 2022 (Gazette 2292/50). Repatriated proceeds may be used for permitted purposes. Goods exporters remain under conversion rules (Rules No. 01 of 2024).

P2_fcy_account.question: Can individuals hold a foreign-currency bank account?
P2_fcy_account.answer: Yes: the Personal Foreign Currency Account (PFCA). Under Foreign Exchange Act Direction No. 04 of 2021 (amended by Direction No. 01 of 2026 regarding government FX debt securities), Sri Lankan nationals, including resident individuals, may hold PFCAs. These can be credited with foreign-exchange remittances received from outside Sri Lanka through the banking system, and debited for outward remittances for current transactions.

L1_registration.question: Must an individual selling digital products or services register a business? How (sole proprietor), cost, online?
L1_registration.answer: Only if you use a trade name. Divisional Secretariat guidance: trading under your full legal name requires no registration, but a trade name must be registered at the Divisional Secretariat within 14 days of starting, under the Business Names Ordinance (Western Province has its own 1990 statute). Registration is in person with a Grama Niladhari report, premises documents and NIC copies. The Colombo DS fee starts at Rs. 500 for start-up capital up to Rs. 300,000. PayHere accepts freelancers without registration (P3); USD payouts need a registered business.

L2_tax_id.question: Tax identification number requirement and how to get it
L2_tax_id.answer: TIN from the Inland Revenue Department. Since 1 January 2024 every individual aged 18 or over must register and get a TIN (Inland Revenue Act s.102). Non-registrants can be registered by the IRD and penalised. Registration is online through IRD e-Services ('Taxpayer Registration', Individual Local) by uploading your NIC; an address proof is needed if your address differs from the NIC.

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: How residents' foreign-sourced or digital income is taxed
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: From 1 April 2025 the income-tax EXEMPTIONS on service exports and foreign-source income were removed (IRD notice PN/IT/2025-01). Instead, a MAXIMUM rate of 15% applies to gains from services rendered in or outside Sri Lanka to anyone, used outside Sri Lanka, where payment is received in foreign currency AND remitted through a bank to Sri Lanka. The same 15% applies to foreign-source income remitted through a bank. Otherwise individuals pay progressive rates: 6% on the first Rs 1,000,000, then 18/24/30%, and 36% on the balance. Personal relief is Rs 1,800,000 from Y/A 2025/26.

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported services and digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: VAT 18% (since 1 Jan 2024). Registration is required only above LKR 15 million in a quarter or LKR 60 million in 12 months; a proposed threshold reduction was ABANDONED (IRD notice, 3 Jul 2026). Zero-rated supplies under s.7 of the VAT Act require payment in foreign currency through a licensed Sri Lankan bank. The SVAT scheme was abolished from 1 Oct 2025. From 1 Jul 2026, foreign platforms supplying services electronically to Sri Lankan customers must charge VAT.

L5_data_protection.question: Data-protection law: name, year, in force?, regulator
L5_data_protection.answer: Personal Data Protection Act No. 9 of 2022, amended by Act No. 22 of 2025 (certified 30 Oct 2025). The amendment made remaining provisions start on dates the Minister appoints by Gazette order. The Data Protection Authority (Part V) has operated since 2023. A Gazette order of 22 July 2026 (No. 2498/16) appoints 1 JANUARY 2027 for Part I (processing of personal data, including a data protection management programme) and Part III (controllers and processors). Data-subject rights (Part II) and penalties (Part VII) await a further order.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; platforms that pay out through PayPal Payouts cannot pay PayPal accounts here (not on PayPal's Payouts list, see P4 for ordinary PayPal receiving). Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts), Polar, Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Creator income through the YouTube Partner Program (available here). (4) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (5) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. (6) Local official channel: Hold a Personal Foreign Currency Account (PFCA). Service-export proceeds must be repatriated within 180 days but are not force-converted, and Payoneer withdraws to an eZ Cash wallet (P1/P2/P5). Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
